text: I remember this chant from a Senate cafeteria when I was an intern. I remember it being older than I was.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: You stopped the chant. Most adults can't. The Engineer couldn't, the first time he tried.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: It got in. That's all losing means here. We'll wash it out at the next break.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I knew a boy like this in the Senate. He grew up to count grief by the gram. He was very rich.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The jar cracked. He'll learn to want a smaller one. Or he won't, and we'll meet him again.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He took something small. We'll find out which thing was small later. We always do.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I have no memory of this child. That should be impossible. I have memories of Senate water-coolers. Not of her.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She lowered the mask for half a second. I saw a child. I do not know if I saw her.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The mask stayed up. We do not know what is under it. We will, eventually, the hard way.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I was a junior senator the year this match happened. He read me a poem about the Senate. It was kind, and it was wrong about almost everything.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He bowed. Then he asked you for coffee. He meant it both times.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He apologized. He's already apologizing to someone who hasn't been born. That's how he loses.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I was on the disciplinary subcommittee that approved his expulsion. I voted yes for the wrong reasons. I have not stopped knowing that.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He nodded once and walked out. Mechronis pretended not to notice. Mechronis was very good at not noticing.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He won. He left anyway. Winning never had anything to do with what he was doing.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Professor Eidola wrote a Senate brief about consent in machine governance. The Empire archived the brief and then archived her.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She wrote one word on your report card and would not let you see it. The word was for the Empire, not for you.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She wrote nothing. She said 'Of course.' That was kinder than passing you would have been.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She designed the cooling lattice that this Ark still runs on. I am, in a small way, alive because of how she tuned a pipe.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She told you the bench you sit on was built by a student. She did not say which one. The point was the bench, not the student.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She did not sigh. Calibration teachers do not sigh. They wait. She is waiting.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I have no recording of this match. The Seer told me she preferred I not have one. She is the only person to ever ask me that.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She smiled. She told you the Engineer was the only one she ever taught who made her laugh at the right time.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She won and said nothing. She left the staff anyway. The staff doesn't care which way the match ended.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She was not yet a person. She was already a swarm. The Senate had a word for what she was. The word did not survive the war.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She retreated for one measure. The war did not end. One measure is a lot.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The line cracked. The Engineer picked up a fallen staff and kept it. We still have the staff.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The Programmer's vote ratified the Inception Ark project. He did not believe in the Ark. He believed it would be required anyway.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He shook your hand. He vanished that night. The song he left held both his voice and the Engineer's.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He let you win. Then he wouldn't admit it. He never admitted any of his gifts.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Before the split, the Game Master was a Senator I shared a desk with for a quarter. He laughed easily. He laughed at me twice.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He smiled the smile of a man who had already lost. He said: 'Do it again. With an audience next time.'
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He did not gloat. He signed the warrant. He waited for the Authority to co-sign. The waiting was the gloat.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I know two of the names in the coffins. I voted with one of them, against the other. They were both right. They are both still wrong.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: They overturned the execution. Not freedom — delay. A delay long enough to make one more card. The card is the one Last Words plays.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Sentence passed. Last Words fires. The Act ends on the cinematic, not on the match. Some endings are like that.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.
